sources.title: How to Play Grand Theft Auto VI in the Cloud and with Remote Play
sources.text: Grand Theft Auto VI supports XBOX Cloud Gaming , making it available to play even without a current-gen console. With XBOX Cloud Gaming, you can play by streaming it straight from the cloud to your XBOX One, or XBOX Series X|S if you’d like to save some hard drive space. Select Game Pass plans include a monthly allotment of up to 15 play hours, and you can buy more cloud playtime if you need it, giving you the opportunity to experience one of the biggest games of the year on the consoles you already own. The game uses XBOX Series S graphics settings when cloud-streamed with XBOX Cloud Gaming. You can also access Remote Play to enjoy Grand Theft Auto VI wherever you want to play , allowing you to stream gameplay directly from your XBOX Series X|S console to devices you already own, like your mobile phone, laptops, PCs, or even a handheld gaming PC like the XBOX ROG Ally. FYI, even wireless networks with high bandwidth can occasionally have a dip in audio and video quality. sources.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 has a 'complex drug network' that tracks everything from where drugs come from to 'how they eventually reach the street-level buyer'
sources.text: "Having that structure in the background as something we consistently refer to helps everything feel more real." I've only dipped my toe into Grand Theft Auto 6 thus far, but I'm already impressed by the detail Rockstar has baked into its world. One thing I'm always curious about with games like this, however, is how much of that detail is on the surface versus what's actually happening under the hood. I'm still too early in the game to judge this for myself, but according to Rockstar, there is way more going on in terms of how NPCs behave than players will ever likely see. One striking example of this is how GTA 6 's gang compounds conduct their drug operations. In an interview with IGN , Rockstar's senior design director for its open world Steven Messinger explained that GTA 6 fully simulates drug distribution from top to bottom. "A big part of [the open world's design] was establishing deep backstories for almost everything, even if they were never meant to be fully explained to the player, and then really sticking to those backstories," Messinger pointed out. "For example, our gang compounds have a complex drug network we've fully mapped out: where the drugs come from, who brings them in and how, how they're distributed to each compound, what happens at each stop, and how they eventually reach the street-level buyer." Messinger notes that "players will only pick up bits and pieces of this". But representing this process wholesale means that, when players do notice it, it always feels authentic and believable. "Having that structure in the background as something we consistently refer to helps everything feel more real, like this big machine is always running even when players aren't there." While this may only be designed for players to notice passively, I'm now keen to follow this system and see just how consistently it holds up. But it's such commitment to representing its world that has led GTA 6 to receive near-universal praise from critics, and it probably didn't hurt when it earned $3.79 billion on launch day , either. 2026 games : All the upcoming games Best PC games : Our all-time favorites Free PC games : Freebie fest Best FPS games : Finest gunplay Best RPGs : Grand adventures Best co-op games : Better together Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team. sources.name: Eurogamer
sources.title: Has Rockstar taken the "Grand Theft Auto" out of GTA 6? Or has it just gamified car-jacking properly for the first time?
sources.text: It's impossible to have a big game launch these days without some section of the internet, somewhere, finding grievances with the final product because it does not align with the expectations they had pre-release. The most recent upset comes in the form of Grand Theft Auto 6 's revised take on, well, grand theft auto. In case you're one of the few still unfamiliar, grand theft auto is more than the titular moniker for Rockstar's premier crime simulation series; it's actually a US legal term for the act of stealing or attempting to steal a motor vehicle. In most previous GTA entries, this was a central part of the core gameplay loop: accept a mission, nick a car, complete the mission, nick another car, getaway. It's an endemic part of the loop, and has become so popular and identifiable as such that even other games - Watch Dogs , Saint's Row, Cyberpunk 2077 , and so on - have emulated the mechanic. So it makes sense that the internet is in a bit of a spin about GTA 6's more mature and restrained take on its eponymous crime. A quick, no-frills getaway in a vehicle you've hijacked on the road isn't always the most effective option. A mindless crime spree on the streets of Leonida is not a simple thing to pull off, nor an easy thing to live down. In this game, actions have consequences, and an ill-timed or ill-judged car jacking can quickly and efficiently put an end to your criminal ambitions. That's not to say you cannot simply steal cars. Of course you can: the option to saunter up to an occupied vehicle and jack it from its registered owner is available to you from the very beginning of the game. But the citizens of Leonida aren't going to take your wanton act of foolishness lying down; many of the motorists in the county will fight back, pull a piece on you, or run you over mid-robbery attempt. Even if you are lucky to find one of the more pliant residents of the city, you might find something peculiar is happening in their car. I jacked a woman in the city over the weekend, and the cat she was ferrying from place to place decided to attack me, causing me to crash. I've heard other people say they've had muffled cries coming from the boot of the car where someone is transporting a hostage, or incidents where they've jacked the same person multiple times, leading to the poor car's owner to have a breakdown in the middle of the city. That cat event, the team here at Eurogamer has worked out, is an early game trigger - it seems stealing random cars early in the game will increase the chance of this encounter occurring. Rockstar's guiding hand is more visible here, then, in trying to teach you a lesson: don't steal cars. You're given your own - Jason's two-door coupé utility, a Vapid Creado - that I actually formed quite an emotional bond with in the opening 10-or-so hours of the game. 'Look after this car,' Rockstar insists, tutorialising you how to repair it, customise it, make it all pretty so it's in good condition when you go pick up Lucia for the first time. Shortly after the 10 hour marker, narrative events whisk you away elsewhere and you're given a 'slim jim', a long, thin tool that allows you to break into locked cars - something you could only do with a quick elbow jab before. The benefit here is two-fold; you can break into cars without setting off their alarms, and without breaking glass and lowering their resale value (something quite important in the earlier sections of the game). So, it takes you until Chapter 2 to start being able to more reliably and consistently break into vehicles. Good. And it'll take even longer to break into keyless vehicles. We're in 2026 after all, and it's heavily implied this is when GTA 6 is also set - it stands to reason that many cars run keyless fobs, and your old-school tools won't cut it if you want to break into a Zorruso, rather than an old Vapid truck. But then, even when you're well-armed and ready to start an illustrious new career as Vice City's most nefarious car thief, there's more to consider. Most modern cars also come with trackers: standard trackers simply prevent you modding cars you don't own (not an issue you'll face very often), but advanced trackers are more problematic. Boosting a car with an advanced tracker immediately alerts the cops to your location, and they close in on you fast . The only answer to this problem is flooring it, and outspeeding the signal ping the tracker is sending out: you need to drive fast and cleanly in order to stay mobile long enough for the tracker to deactivate, and this often incurs damage that makes selling these cars to fences a less viable option. You can't even sell cars with trackers installed at all to some fences until you're much, much further into the game. So, long story short, stealing cars is a faff in GTA 6. But I like that. I like that Rockstar has evolved the gameplay formula to more accurately reflect the state of the world in 2026. Modern problems require modern answers, and given that Rockstar has gone above and beyond in its creation of a sandbox simulation of Florida , I feel the immersion would be broken by just being able to saunter up to any car you want and break into it. No, needing a 'slim jim' or a key cloner - or needing to case my victims properly before trying to jack them - makes for a better game as far as I'm concerned. It makes me roleplay Jason and Lucia better, it makes me engage with the game's systems more, it makes me appreciate the cars that I do have whilst I have them. It also improves the flow of the game and how I interact with missions. I recently played GTA: Vice City , and after most missions were wrapped up, I would simply fling the nearest motorist onto the sidewalk, hop in their car, and drive away into the Malibu-styled sunset. I can't simply do that in GTA 6: I need to think about my getaway options, whether there's heat on my car, and where my next best (and cheapest) ride is going to be if a robbery or raid goes awry. sources.title: The Grand Theft Auto 6 hacker who was hospitalized in 2023 has been released on parole with a warning not to do it again
sources.text: Following his guilty plea, Arion Kurtaj was given a seven-year sentence but released "on license" with a warning and restrictions to his online activity.. A BBC report says Arion Kurtaj, the Grand Theft Auto 6 leaker who was given an indefinite sentence in hospital in 2023 because he kept hacking into things or expressing intent to, has been released with a stern warning not to do it again. Kurtaj was sentenced to seven years in prison, according to the report, but was released on license—similar to parole in North America—the same day, with his hospital stay and time in prison while awaiting retrial credited as time served. He was given a five-year "Serious Crime Prevention Order" restricting his allowable online activity, including bans on using Telegram and Discord. "Kurtaj knew what he was doing when he carried out these crimes and has finally admitted his involvement," Detective Inspector Mike O'Sullivan of the City of London Police said following Kurtaj's sentencing and release. "We hope this case serves as a lesson that these types of acts will not be tolerated. "Although cyber crime is borderless, we will seek to utilise the co-operation of partner agencies and international law enforcement to ensure that offenders are brought to justice no matter where they offend from." Kurtaj carried out hacks against multiple companies when he was 16 and 17 years old, including Microsoft , Samsung , Nvidia and UK telecom company BT&EE, and stole millions in cryptocurrency from individuals. But it was his hack of Rockstar and leak of GTA 6 materials more than a year before it was formally revealed, that earned him notoriety, not least because of how it was carried out: While under police protection in a Travelodge hotel room , using an Amazon Fire Stick and a mobile phone. A psychiatric assessment determined that Kurtaj had "acute autism," and that he "continued to express the intent to return to cybercrime as soon as possible" while he was in custody. That led to his hospital sentence , but earlier this year he was found fit to stand trial and subsequently pleaded guilty to all charges . That struck me as odd—why plead guilty to crimes carried out at a time when your mental state was such that a court decided you required multiple years of institutionalization?—but this may be the answer: Kurtaj, now 21, is a free man. The judge on the case told Kurtaj he is "a very talented young man," but also warned him: "Don't let this happen again." sources.title: Grand Theft Auto VI for PS5 tops 39 million players
sources.text: More than 39 million unique users have played Grand Theft Auto VI on PlayStation 5 as of November 22, making it the biggest launch in PlayStation history across three decades and five console generations, Sony Interactive Entertainment announced . The sequel set a new record for the highest number of concurrent players for any game on PlayStation, surpassing previous records across multiplayer, free-to-play, and single-player titles. Across PlayStation 5, players cumulatively logged 683 million hours of gameplay in Grand Theft Auto VI , and have spent an average of 17.4 hours exploring the game’s world during its opening days. Grand Theft Auto VI ‘s launch also marked the largest number of newly connected PlayStation 5 consoles on a single day since the console’s launch, outside of end-of-year holidays. Since launch, it was the first played game on 70 percent of new PlayStation 5 consoles. “We want to congratulate our partners at Rockstar Games for bringing this extraordinary game to players around the world and continuing a partnership with PlayStation that stretches back to Grand Theft Auto III on PlayStation 2 ,” Sony Interactive Entertainment content communications manager Tim Turi said. “With [ Grand Theft Auto VI ], we worked to bring the best experience on [PlayStation 5] and gave players a memorable way to commemorate the game with two special limited-edition DualSense wireless controllers inspired by Vice City. We also celebrated the launch with live events including Grand Theft Auto VI : The Festival in Miami this past weekend.” Grand Theft Auto VI launched for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series on November 19. On November 20, Rockstar Games announced that the game achieved $3.79 billion in day one retail sales following 32.5 million pre-sales. Although Rockstar Games did not share exact unit numbers, the revenue total suggests roughly 37.9 million to 47.3 million copies sold, based solely on pricing across its $79.99 and $99.99 editions.

sources.text: Grand Theft Auto games have always been the perfect place to let loose and cause a little chaos, with their expansive open worlds giving you plenty of freedom to do whatever you want. GTA 6 is no different, and while there’s plenty of fun to be had completing missions and planning heists, sometimes you just want to cause some mayhem, spawn vehicles, or get your hands on some easy cash. That’s where cheat codes come in. Cheats have been a staple of the Grand Theft Auto franchise for decades, and you probably remember scribbling down your favourite combinations on a piece of paper to keep them close at hand. Thankfully, GTA 6 makes things a little easier, with a range of cheats available to shake up your experience and offer some unique ways to explore Vice City. Whether you’re looking to spawn vehicles, unlock special abilities, or simply wreak havoc across the map, here’s a complete breakdown of every GTA 6 cheat code and what each one does. You can buy Grand Theft Auto 6 here if you haven’t already! There are 61 cheats to use in Grand Theft Auto 6, ranging from combat and player cheats to vehicle spawns and environmental changes. It’s important to note that these cheats can only be used after completing the main story, with most requiring you to meet certain unlock requirements. What’s more pressing, though, is that inputting any cheat code will disable trophies and achievements from unlocking , as well as saving the game—but only for the remainder of that play session. Only use these if you’re looking to kick back and mess around, as they won’t help you progress in any way. To input cheat codes in GTA 6, you’ll need to use the in-game phone by pressing up on the D-Pad, then hold L1/LB and press R1/RB followed by the cheat input. You’ll know that cheats are unlocked and usable, as a new Cheats List menu will appear under the Progress Menu. This won’t appear during the story, once again showing that you’ll need to beat the main game first. Of course, each cheat has its own input you’ll need to use, and they range from giving instant money to making you drunk—a true variety. You’ll find the full list of cheat codes below. sources.name: Eurogamer
sources.title: Rockstar is actively shopping Read Dead Redemption movie and TV rights around, just don't expect the same for Grand Theft Auto
sources.text: Rockstar Games is seemingly interested in expanding Red Dead Redemption beyond video games, after years of Hollywood knocking on its doors. According to a new report, the company is looking for someone to pick up the movie and TV rights for its open-world Westerner series. The information comes from a new report in The Ankler , citing agents in the know. According to the report, Rockstar wanted something in the range of $100m (£76m) as a minimum for the license to its Red Dead Redemption series of games. As the report pointed out, Amazon paid $250m (£191m) in 2017 for Lord of the Rings' TV show rights alone. Rockstar, however, is not interested in turning Grand Theft Auto into a movie or TV show, per the same report. It's not clear why the company is willing to entertain the idea for one franchise and not the other, but the vastly larger popularity of GTA (compared to RDR, at least) could explain why. It's worth noting that streamers like Netflix and Amazon have been on something of a hot streak recently with the success of shows based on popular video games, such as Fallout . HBO managed to turn The Last of Us into a prestige series that can attract both fans of the game and casual TV viewers. Indeed, many more video game-based shows are in the works, like Amazon's Tomb Raider series , its God of War adaptation , as well as FX's Far Cry anthology show . Even Call of Duty, a massive - though nowhere near as massive as GTA - franchise, is getting a live-action movie in 2028 . But none of those are as profitable or culturally-dominnant as Grand Theft Auto. GTA 6 just released, and immediately beat analyst expectations. The game made $3.79bn (£2.90bn) in revenue on day one off the back of 32.5m copies sold, making it the biggest launch of any entertainment product in history, so it's understandable why Rockstar is not too eager to turn it into a movie or TV show.

sources.title: God of War Laufey's Faye actor jumps from games to live-action, as Amazon casts Deborah Ann Woll in upcoming series
sources.text: After appearing in both God of War Ragnarok and next year's God of War Laufey, Deborah Ann Woll is about to reprise her role as Faye in Amazon Prime Video's upcoming live-action series. Variety reports that the God of War cast list is now welcoming a second actor pulled straight from Sony Santa Monica's video game series. Deborah Ann Woll first showed up in the games as Kratos' wife and Atreus' mother during God of War Ragnarok, but she's also about to enter the spotlight proper in God of War Laufey. Amazon's God of War cast now includes Dave Bautista (Guardians of the Galaxy) as god killer Kratos, Callum Vinson (Chucky) as Atreus, Mandy Patinkin as Odin and Ólafur Darri Ólafsson as Thor. Alastair Duncan is also making the game-to-show jump by stepping back into the figurative shoes of chatty head Mimir. Earlier in the year, the God of War show halted production when former Kratos actor Ryan Hurst suffered an on-set injury. Bautista soon took over the role and production began again in October - all of Hurst's scenes had to be reshot, of course. There's no release date yet for the show, but it's said to follow the Norse era of the games which began in 2018's more serious and stern revamp. Amazon ordered a two-season run for the show, which apparently means both seasons will be filmed back-to-back. Meanwhile, God of War Laufey was recently delayed from February 2027 to May 2027, giving the PS5 exclusive slightly more breathing room away from Fable, Persona 4 Revival and Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis. "We will make the most of each moment until then by putting in the finishing touches and pushing the game to its fullest potential," developer Sony Santa Monica said at the time. "On behalf of everyone on the team, we appreciate your patience and we'll be back to share more updates soon." While the game puts Faye in the leading role as she battles with gods in a multi-mythological afterlife, the studio was quick to note that her journey isn't considered a side game. God of War Laufey will still connect to future games in the series and, yep, Kratos will eventually be back , too. "Genuinely, I thought I was going to be much more offended by it, but one, I'm not on social media, so that helps, and two, I don't know, I feel totally unbothered," Woll said of the online trolls who were targeting Laufey after its reveal this summer. "Because I just know it's great. It's okay if it's not your cup of tea, but in no universe is it bad."

sources.title: PS5 Games on Sale for $15 for Black Friday
sources.text: In the olden days (a few years ago) you had to wait until the actual day of Black Friday before the killer deals would crop up. Those days are officially gone. Today, on the Monday before Black Friday official, Walmart kicked off its “ Black Friday Event 2 ,” dropping some absolutely killer deals, and Amazon is price matching most of them. Among the discounts are a bunch of PS5 games on sale for just $15. These games are excellent and not that old. So grab what you want, because you’re not likely to find them cheaper any time soon. What games are we talking? For starters, Mafia: The Old Country, an excellent single-player game that came out last year that our reviewer called “an effective return to the linear and tightly story-driven format of the original Mafia and Mafia II.” Then there’s Assassin’s Creed Shadows , in which Ubisoft’s long-running series finally goes to Japan. We gave it an 8/10 in our review , saying, “By sharpening the edges of its existing systems, Assassin’s Creed Shadows creates one of the best versions of the open-world style it’s been honing for the last decade.” Then there’s Borderlands 4 and Star Wars Outlaws and WWE 2K26, all fine games worth checking out if you haven’t already. Fifteen bucks will even get you Elden Ring, Fromsoft’s sprawling, open-world masterpiece that we gave a 10/10 in our review when it came out in 2022. That same year, we awarded it Game of the Year . Other all-time low prices can be had now as well, like AirPods Pro 3 for $149 and Metal Gear Solid Master Collection Vol 2. for $29.99 . sources.title: Black Friday PlayStation: jogos de PS5 e PS4 têm descontos de até 74%; veja preços
sources.text: A PlayStation anunciou uma campanha de Black Friday e fim de ano no Brasil, com descontos em jogos, acessórios e dispositivos para PS5 e PS4 . As ofertas começaram em 20 de novembro e seguem até 24 de dezembro de 2026 , nas principais redes de varejo autorizadas. Entre os destaques estão o PlayStation VR2 , com redução de R$ 700, controles DualSense com descontos de até 20% e jogos em mídia física com preços a partir de R$ 59,90. A campanha também contempla títulos recentes, como Marvel’s Wolverine , Ghost of Yōtei e Death Stranding 2: On the Beach . O PlayStation VR2 é um dos principais destaques da campanha. O dispositivo de realidade virtual para PS5 teve seu preço sugerido reduzido de R$ 3.499,90 para R$ 2.799,90 , uma economia de R$ 700. Os controles DualSense também estão com preços promocionais, incluindo modelos tradicionais e edições especiais. Confira os principais valores anunciados: Os descontos contemplam diferentes opções de cores e modelos, conforme a disponibilidade nas lojas participantes. Os jogos em mídia física também fazem parte da campanha, com descontos que chegam a 74%. O maior percentual anunciado é para LEGO Horizon Adventures , que passa a custar R$ 59,90 . Já títulos como Marvel’s Spider-Man 2 , God of War Ragnarök e The Last of Us Part I , normalmente vendidos por R$ 399,90, aparecem com preço sugerido de R$ 169,90. Confira alguns dos principais jogos em promoção: Outros jogos, como Marvel’s Spider-Man: Miles Morales , Uncharted: Coleção Legado dos Ladrões , Sackboy: Uma Grande Aventura e Death Stranding Versão do Diretor , têm preço sugerido de R$ 114,90 . A campanha inclui lançamentos recentes e edições especiais do catálogo de PS5. Segundo a PlayStation, Marvel’s Wolverine participa da campanha com desconto de até 30%. Quem ainda utiliza o PlayStation 4 também encontra ofertas na campanha. Jogos da linha PlayStation Hits, como God of War , Bloodborne , The Last of Us Remasterizado , Until Dawn e Uncharted: The Nathan Drake Collection , estão com preço sugerido de R$ 59,90 . O mesmo valor vale para Ghost of Tsushima e Death Stranding . Já God of War Ragnarök , The Last of Us Part II , Gran Turismo 7 e Days Gone aparecem por R$ 114,90 . A campanha começou em 20 de novembro e termina em 24 de dezembro de 2026 . Os descontos estão disponíveis nas principais redes de varejo autorizadas do Brasil, conforme a disponibilidade de estoque. sources.text: It’s the first time Nintendo’s racing sequel has been re-released in 25 years Nintendo has added a 12th title to the GameCube library on Nintendo Switch Online. Wave Race: Blue Storm is the latest game which can be found in the console’s Nintendo Classics: GameCube app, which is available as part of a Nintendo Switch Online + Expansion Pass subscription. A launch title for the GameCube when it was released in late 2001, Wave Race: Blue Storm is the third game in the Wave Race series, after the Game Boy original and its iconic sequel Wave Race 64. Success in its races involve navigating between red and yellow buoys, which builds up the player’s turbo meter and makes it possible to get speed boosts. The game also had a cheat code which let you unlock a sarcastic announcer who would insult the player all the time. Some of his comments can be heard in the new trailer for the Switch 2 release, seen below. The addition of Wave Race: Blue Storm brings the total number of GameCube games on Switch 2 to 12, meaning the full list is now as follows: Nintendo also previously announced that PokÃ©mon Colosseum is coming to the library, but hasnât yet confirmed its release date. sources.name: Eurogamer
sources.title: Modders already have GTA 6 running on PC, after CyberLeek released a full Xbox build of the game
sources.text: A PC version of Grand Theft Auto 6 - one from unofficial sources, at least - may be closer than we thought. After suddenly returning last week with a near-full build of the Xbox version , notorious leaker CyberLeek has now posted the missing piece they intentionally held back: the game's executable (.exe) file. "The exe is out. Always free. An early Christmas gift from CL," CyberLeek reportedly wrote, as relayed on Reddit . "The torch passes to the open source re-comp and emulation projects." Hours later, the recompilation modders and hackers part of the Project Leonida Discord server - the current hub for all GTA 6 recompilation efforts - posted footage of the game booting up on PC. In just a matter of hours, modders - with the help of Claude AI - managed to turn the leaked Xbox build into a PC port, of sorts. In this Reddit video , you can see the game boot up to the initial setup before hitting a black screen. The build is clearly not yet playable, though Eurogamer has not directly verified those claims. Shayder, one of the lead developers on Project Leonida, said in a since-deleted post on X that we should "expect a lot of static recompilation work to be done soon." On the project's Discord server, they later clarified that it could take about a week for the build to reach a playable state on PC. As for CyberLeek, the leaker is still soliciting donations for a secret project "for the gamers", adding in the build's readme file , "Nobody has to give anything, and every release stays free either way. But every donation is a vote for more of this, and so is every trade of the token." Rockstar has not announced a PC version of GTA 6, but the company has historically released its games on PC several months after their console debut. In October, a report said GTA 6's PC version would arrive in the first quarter of 2027 , an unusually short gap between the console and PC releases. These latest recompilation efforts, however, may force Rockstar to speed up development of the PC version. Though the recompiled build may never reach the level of quality or stability of an official port, many of those eager to play the game on PC likely wouldn't care.

sources.title: How to get the GTA 6 BF Bandito
sources.text: You won't find the BF Bandito in a lock up in GTA 6, as this vehicle heist is a little tricker to pull off While you're out stealing cars for Moses, the GTA 6 BF Bandito will appear on your list, taking you out to the very rural roads of South Leonard County and the Buckskin Swamp. This GTA 6 heist is slightly harder than the others you might have carried out so far though, as this car will be on the move. Like all of Moses' targets, the rough location of the BF Bandito is marked on the map, but as you make your way there, you'll pass by some whoopin' and hollerin' country dwellers who are already taking the buggy for a spin. Here's how to get your hands on the GTA 6 Bandito and get paid. The map marker will take you to the rough location of the BF Bandito, where you should keep your eyes and ears open for some locals riding around the swamps on buggies - one of these is the Bandito. To claim it for yourself, you'll need to stop the Bandito driver, and there are a few ways to do this. If you clock him fast enough, particularly when crossing water, you can simply get in front of him, and he'll stop. Otherwise, you can chase down the Bandito, shooting the driver and his pals. Weirdly, though, when I did this challenge, the driver eventually just stopped and bolted, leaving the buggy free for me to take, though I'm not sure exactly what triggered him to do this. Essentially, just stay close, don't destroy the car by shooting it too much, and it'll be yours in no time. sources.name: GameSpot
sources.title: Xbox Project Helix Was Reportedly Designed To Make Online Multiplayer Free

sources.name: GamesRadar
sources.title: Xbox Project Helix was reportedly planned to run Steam games and have free online multiplayer
sources.text: It might've mirrored Valve's own Steam Machine Xbox Project Helix , the next (mysterious) console underway from Microsoft , has been in the limelight recently for its support of PC games – support that was reportedly far more fleshed out during the hardware's initial conception. Jason Ronald, vice president of Xbox's gaming devices and ecosystem team, recently said that Project Helix is "a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC," as "it's really designed to be the ultimate gaming machine." That sounds pretty dang capable already, but apparently, it was supposed to feature even more PC integration – think full-on free online multiplayer access, Steam, and the like. Anonymous sources tell Windows Central as much, alleging that the original plan – one operating underneath a different codename – for the console was for it to essentially be a gaming computer that can also run Xbox games… on top of PC titles on storefronts like Valve 's own Steam. Think the ASUS ROG Xbox Ally , for example, albeit not handheld. I'm reminded of the Steam Machine, personally, although that notably doesn't run on Windows. The supposed predecessor to Project Helix would work with a gamepad-centered Xbox-style full-screen interface (like Steam's Big Picture Mode, for example), allowing users to exit out to a normal Windows desktop and run other programs such as Steam. Furthermore, the report states the console would've been free to play online – no extra subscriptions or fees like Sony 's PlayStation Plus service required to engage in multiplayer games. That would mean no Xbox Game Pass paywall, as a PC wouldn't… well, work with a paywall at all, really. This wouldn't have been a cheap decision for Microsoft, and that paired with a move toward another hardware strategy, changes in management, and more, likely contributed to a reshuffle of plans – if this intriguing computer-esque console ever truly was on the table, that is. It does all beg the question: what will Project Helix look like? I suppose we won't know until it's finally here. Let's just hope it doesn't cost as much as $1,800 – one rumored price point I can't quite get out of my head. For now, I think I'll just stick to my good ol' actual PC. Hardware nerds unite, sign up to our free tech newsletter for a weekly digest of the hottest new tech, the latest gadgets on the test bench, and much more from the team at GamesRadar+. Xbox Project Helix lead says it's "one of the most exciting times" to be making a new console, because the "challenging" component crisis means finding new ways to balance innovation and accessibility After spending years with her head in various fantastical realms' clouds, Anna studied English Literature and then Medieval History at the University of Edinburgh, going on to specialize in narrative design and video game journalism as a writer. She has written for various publications since her postgraduate studies, including Dexerto, Fanbyte, GameSpot, IGN, PCGamesN, and more. When she's not frantically trying to form words into coherent sentences, she's probably daydreaming about becoming a fairy druid and befriending every animal or she's spending a thousand (more) hours traversing the Underdark in Baldur's Gate 3. If you spot her away from her PC, you'll always find Anna with a fantasy book, a handheld video game console of some sort, and a Tamagotchi or two on hand. sources.name: Eurogamer
sources.title: Microsoft reportedly looked into killing paid multiplayer for next-gen Xbox Helix consoles
sources.text: A new report from Windows Central details how Xbox was reportedly looking into removing the paywall that prevents players without Xbox Live from playing online games, only to potentially renege on its decision sometime during production of the next-gen device. "Sources close to Microsoft's plans tell me Xbox Helix was originally conceived as a true console-PC hybrid with access to Windows PC games and stores such as Steam, alongside another major change: no paywall for online multiplayer," says the Windows Central report. It goes on to note that this Xbox Live-free plan was iterated upon under Xbox's previous leadership, but with Asha Sharma's appointment as Xbox head in February , all that apparently changed. I guess she did promise "radically different business models" , after all. The revised plan has reportedly been altered thanks to a myriad of factors affecting the Xbox business: new management, rising component costs, and a shifting hardware strategy, are all outlined specifically in the report. We've previously heard that Xbox's next-gen console could cost up to $1,800 , with a handheld version coming in 2027 and a full release by holiday 2028 (a Helix console at $1,200 would mean a 50 percent increase on top of Series X's current price, for what it's worth). Sharma has stressed Helix will launch as "a family of devices" that will act as a bridge between PC and Xbox capable of playing games from both platforms . If Xbox has, indeed, decided to scrap the idea of free online multiplayer access, it'll be a blow to the idealistic 'PC and Xbox' platform that Microsoft has been touting for the past few years: PC players do not need a subscription in order to access online modes, so - right out the gate - there will be a division between one group of players and the other. Perhaps this is why we've heard a little change in the tone of how Sharma and other Xbox bosses are talking about Helix more recently - these hints that the console will be a true PC-and-console hybrid have died down, and been replaced by insinuations that we'll see more of a traditional console with the "ability to play your PC games." Xbox has been running Xbox Live as a service since 2002, when it launched on the original Xbox console. By 2005, it was split into gold and silver tiers to distinguish free players from those that paid. In 2023, the service was fully renamed Xbox Game Pass Core , looping in access to the base roster of Game Pass games with online play.

sources.title: How to steal the Declasse Vamos in GTA 6
sources.text: Grab the code to unlock the garage and steal the car for Moses. The Declasse Vamos is one of the many cars Moses asks you to steal for him in GTA 6 , but like the BF Bandito , it's a little trickier than just grabbing it. When you reach the map marker, you'll realise the car is locked in a garage that requires a specific code to open it. The code to the door is 2727 and this is fixed. The way you discover this is by sneaking inside the trailer and looking at the number plate on the wall to the left of the window, just above the guy snoozing in the chair. Enter the code to open the garage, break in with the slimjim, then hit the button to open the door. I personally incapacitated all of the people behind the trailer, so chances are they will pursue you or start shooting if you don't, once you try to drive out of there. Now take the car back to Moses, being careful on the way, to earn $4,100ish for top condition. sources.title: How to steal the Schafter V12 in GTA 6
sources.text: Prove yourself to Raul by yoinking this car. Stealing the Schafter V12 in GTA 6 is one of the car theft missions you'll have to complete to gain Raul's trust, but similar to the BF Bandito or Declasse Vamos , it's a little tricky. Make sure to grab the silenced pistol from the trunk of the car outside—not necessarily because you'll need it, but because it's a handy weapon to have. Now, as you can see in the video above, you can get into the chop shop by climbing up the van around back and then onto the roof. I'd then suggest dropping down on the right side, where there are few enemies, knocking out the guy sitting by the gate, then opening it by hitting the left button. Sneak back towards the centre of the chop shop and turn left to find the Declasse Vamos, a black unassuming car. Hop inside, start it up, and drive out of the gate you just opened. Easy, right? Now simply bring it to Randy's garage as directed. You also kill everyone inside if you wish, but my way above will get you that non-lethal Criminal Profile rating. sources.title: GTA 6 Car Service walkthrough: How to steal the Schafter V12
sources.text: Wondering how to steal the Schafter V12 in GTA 6? In this GTA 6 Chapter 3 mission, Lucia steals a luxury car from a gang-run chop shop and delivers it to one of Raulâs contacts. This mission also introduces you to Randy, a new vehicle drop-off point. Here’s everything you need to know about completing Car Service in GTA 6, including how to find the Schafter V12, escape the police and earn your reward. Need even more GTA 6 guides for Chapter 3 of Grand Theft Auto 6 ? Then check out our GTA 6 Guide Hub . Guides: If you're playing Grand Theft Auto 6, make sure to checkÂ out ourÂ complete walkthrough hub , featuringÂ beginner tips , navigation experience explained , GTA 6 cheats , and more. In GTA 6, Car Service becomes available after completing the Meet the Heders mission . Once you’ve finished, wait approximately one in-game day for a message from Raul. You’ll then receive a new mission marker in Vice City, where Lucia is tasked with stealing a Benefactor Schafter V12 from a gang hideout. Before entering the chop shop, look for a nearby vehicle with equipment stored in its trunk. Inside, you’ll find a silenced Klose K17 pistol and flash grenades. The silenced pistol is perfect for this next section, as the chop shop is pretty open plan, and thus difficult to stealth through. Head towards the compound and look for a white van. Climb onto its roof to access the metal roofing surrounding the yard.Â From here, you can survey the area and keep an eye on the gang members guarding the entrance. Be careful around the dog near the gates, as attacking it unnecessarily can negatively affect your criminal profile. The car is parked underneath the covered section in the middle of the chop shop, next to a small room. If you want to verify it’s the correct car,Â you can scan it with the WAINK app. Head towards the vehicle, deal with any remaining guards and get behind the wheel. Drive out of the compound and escape the area. You don’t actually have to take out the guards, you can just leave with the car, but taking out the guards makes it much easier, and doesn’t risk destroying the car, which will fail the mission. Once you’ve escaped, follow the GPS route to Leonida Auto World, where Randy is waiting.Drive into the dealership’s parking area to trigger the final cutscene and complete the mission. The reward for completing Car Service earns you $3,000 and unlocks Randy as a vehicle drop-off point. He can purchase certain vehicles you bring him, including cars with standard trackers and vehicles on his request list.

sources.name: Gematsu
sources.title: Acts of Blood for PC delayed to spring 2027
sources.text: Publisher Big Fan Games and developer Eksil Team have delayed beat ’em up action game Acts of Blood from its previously planned December 4, 2026 release to spring 2027 for PC via Steam and Microsoft Store . PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series versions are also due out in 2027. Here is the full message from Eksil Team on the delay: With heavy heart we’re making a difficult decision to postpone the release of the game on PC (Steam) into spring 2027. We know the decision might disappoint for you, whom already looking forward to play our game on December. But after assessing the feedback we got from players, play testers, and internal team, we found several issues that still can be improved with a little bit more time, and hopefully it will deliver the best experience we intended.
